title: VU#580079: Arbitrary file read/write vulnerability in ImageMagick-based applications with default configuration
content_md: Overview Multiple arbitrary file read and write vulnerabilities have been identified in applications that use ImageMagick with insufficiently restrictive security policies. Collectively referred to as ImageTragick2 , these issues arise when ImageMagick processes attacker-controlled SVG or PostScript content using dangerous coders or delegates permitted by its default or application-supplied configuration. An attacker who can upload an image, or otherwise cause an application to process crafted image content, may be able to read or write files accessible to the ImageMagick process. In some deployments, these capabilities may be chained to achieve arbitrary code execution, compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected application and host. Description ImageMagick is a widely used open-source image-processing suite. Web and content-management applications, including Ruby on Rails, WordPress, MediaWiki, ownCloud Classic, and Redmine, may use ImageMagick for operations such as thumbnail generation, cropping, conversion, and transformation. ImageMagick is also commonly included in containerized AI image-processing pipelines. It may operate before inference to normalize or transform inputs, or after inference to convert and prepare generated output. In these environments, images may originate not only from direct uploads but also from URLs, automated agents, datasets, model outputs, or other upstream services.
